subject: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paygrid.com>, Sophie Chang <sophie.chang@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps

Hi Alex / Sophie

Great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Objective: validate whether open models can reach parity with PayGrid’s current proprietary baseline for invoice parsing + QA assistant workflows. High-level acceptance: human-eval pass rate within 5 percentage points of your baseline on the 1k sample set, and no major regression on critical entity extraction (vendor, amount, invoice_date).

2) Recommended evaluation plan (attached): prompt set (paygrid_prompt_set_v1.zip) + eval_template.csv. Marissa will run the Redwood evaluation harness and produce both automatic metrics and a small human-eval.

3) Initial model candidates:
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized fp4) - low cost, good precision on short QA tasks
   - Llama-2-70B-chat (int8/4-bit) - higher accuracy for long-context invoice-heavy prompts
   - A finetuned Llama-2-13B variant (our internal tuned checkpoint) as an intermediate option

4) Key constraints you raised: latency target <= 300ms median per token for interactive QA; data residency: US only for this pilot.

5) Next steps:
   - Alex: share a redacted 1k sample (or allow Redwood to sample from production staging) - target by Wed 3/3
   - Marissa: start automated eval once sample received, share preliminary metrics within 3 business days
   - Lauren/Aditya: provide benchmark links and recommended inference configs (quant, batching, cache settings)

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v1.zip, eval_template.csv

If that looks correct I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up to review results and discuss acceptance criteria + potential pricing for a Dedicated eval.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Chang <sophie.chang@paygrid.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps

Thanks Lauren, appreciate the clear plan. A couple quick questions before we hand over the sample: 

- Can you confirm expected cost and latency ranges for the two model families above for our 1k eval? Sophie and I need rough TCO to budget the pilot.
- For the human-eval, what instructions will the raters follow? We want to ensure directionals align with our internal QA.

We can get a redacted 1k by EOD Wed (3/3) if that works. Also looping in our security contact offline for data handing questions.

Best,
Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Products
PayGrid
alex.rivera@paygrid.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paygrid.com>, Sophie Chang <sophie.chang@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps

Alex — quick answers inline: 

- Cost/Latency: rough estimates for the 1k eval (on Redwood Hosted test cluster):
   * Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp4 quantized): ~$45 total compute; median per-token latency ~120ms; end-to-end per-invoice 300-450ms depending on prompt length
   * Llama-2-70B-chat (int8): ~$320 total compute; median per-token latency ~280ms; better long-context stability

These numbers assume our default batching/config; if you need Dedicated baseline we can produce more stable throughput numbers.

- Human-eval instructions: we’ll use a two-rater scheme. Primary checks: critical entity correctness (vendor, total, invoice_date), then a 5-point quality scale for overall answer usefulness. We’ll share the exact rubric in the Drive folder (link below).

Related links: evaluation rubric + prior parity report: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bPayGridEval

Marissa will confirm timeline once sample is in. We’re good to proceed on Wed.

Thanks,
Lauren

P.S. Aditya — can you attach the quick parity-run script (small) and recommended quant settings to the folder?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paygrid.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps

Hi all,

Per Lauren’s plan I put together a short eval SOP and acceptance thresholds for transparency. Summary below and attached CSV is the eval_template.csv we’ll use to report results.

Eval plan (automated + human):
- Dataset: PayGrid redacted 1k invoice sample (we’ll keep a 10% holdout for final QA).
- Models to run: Mistral-Instruct-7B (fp4), Llama-2-13B-finetuned (int8/4bit), Llama-2-70B-chat (int8).
- Metrics: entity exact-match (vendor, total, invoice_date); token-level F1 for extraction; human-eval usefulness (1-5).
- Acceptance thresholds (pilot pass):
   * Entity exact-match >= 92% for vendor and total OR within 5 percentage points of PayGrid baseline
   * Human-eval average >= 4.2/5 OR within 0.05 of your baseline mean
   * No critical regression on edge-case formats (PO numbers, multi-line totals) - see flags in eval_template.csv

Timeline: once we have the 1k sample: automated run + preliminary metrics in 48-72 hours; human-eval + consolidated report within 5 business days.

Security note: please confirm if the sample will be uploaded to the shared Drive or if you prefer an SFTP drop. We can also provide a short redaction script if helpful.

Attachments: eval_template.csv

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Chang <sophie.chang@paygrid.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid - model fit evals & parity next steps

Thanks team — this all looks good. We’ll upload the redacted 1k to the shared Drive by EOD today (link will go to the folder you shared). A few notes:

- We’re okay with the acceptance thresholds as written; if a model hits the thresholds we’ll schedule a demo of the system in production-like settings.
- On latency: if Mistral hits thresholds but Llama-70 shows higher latency we’re open to a hybrid approach (Mistral for interactive QA, Llama-70 for batch reconciliation). Please document the hybrid recommendation in the final report.
- Sophie will coordinate with our procurement team should we need a Dedicated eval contract.

Let’s tentatively schedule the results review for next Wed 3/16 — Lauren, can you send a calendar invite?

Appreciate the fast turnaround,
Alex

--
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Products, PayGrid
alex.rivera@paygrid.com
